title: Sourav Ganguly and Wife Dona File Police Complaint After Six Months of Death Threat Letters
excerpt: The former India captain lodged a formal complaint in Kolkata after couriered letters escalated from fan mail to explicit threats against his family.
body:
• Former India cricket captain Sourav Ganguly and his wife Dona filed a formal police complaint in Kolkata on August 10 after receiving death threat letters over the past six months.
  • The latest threatening letter, written in English, contained explicit threats to eliminate Ganguly and his family, escalating from earlier communications dismissed as fan mail.
  • Each letter arrived via courier with the sender identified as Arun Kumar from Belgharia; police are investigating whether the name is genuine or being used as cover.
  • West Bengal's state security department has been notified and is assessing whether Ganguly's existing security arrangements need to be strengthened.

Former India cricket captain Sourav Ganguly and his wife Dona Ganguly have filed a formal police complaint in Kolkata after receiving death threats through a series of couriered letters spanning six months.

Letters Escalated From Hate Mail to Death Threats

The complaint was lodged at Thakurpukur Police Station on August 10, the same day the most recent threatening letter was opened at Ganguly's office as president of the Cricket Association of Bengal (CAB).

https://youtube.com/watch?v=zw4JYL5hpuE

The latest letter, composed entirely in English, carried explicit language threatening to "finish" Ganguly and his family. Two letters arrived addressed separately to Sourav and Dona Ganguly, containing what the complaint described as "hate remarks" alongside "serious threats to the life and safety" of the couple and people working with them.

"The nature of the threats contained in the letters has caused serious concern among us. Since the letters have now escalated from hate/derogatory communication to explicit threats to life and personal safety, we believe that the matter requires immediate police intervention and investigation."

— Statement from Ganguly's complaint

Earlier letters in the series had been treated as correspondence from overzealous fans, but the increasingly menacing tone of the most recent communication prompted the family to seek formal police intervention.

Police Launch Investigation

All the letters arrived via courier at the Ganguly household, with the sender identified as Arun Kumar, listed as a resident of Belgharia, a locality in North 24 Parganas district near Kolkata. Investigators traced a phone number included in one of the letters, and a Truecaller search returned the same name.

https://x.com/avbvikash1810/status/2087082039338266743

Police are now working to determine whether the actual Arun Kumar dispatched the letters or whether a third party has been misusing his identity to send the threats.

"We have started an investigation and are taking all necessary measures to ensure the safety of Mr. Ganguly and his family," police officials said in response to the complaint.

Security Review Under Way

West Bengal's state security department was notified immediately following the complaint and has been directed to respond without delay. The department is currently assessing whether Ganguly's existing security arrangements need strengthening, given the sustained nature of the threats over half a year.

Ganguly has had government security since 2002, when threats of violence from unidentified militants first prompted the West Bengal state government to provide round-the-clock protection to the cricketer.

A Turbulent Year for Ganguly Off the Field

The death threats are the latest in a string of security and legal concerns for the former BCCI president. In June, Ganguly filed a separate complaint at the same police station against an unofficial Facebook page with 3.6 million followers that he alleged was spreading false and defamatory content, including fabricated claims of an Enforcement Directorate raid on his home. His wife Dona had previously lodged a complaint in late 2025 over body-shaming and abusive remarks on social media following her Odissi dance performance at the Kolkata International Film Festival.

Ganguly captained India from 2000 to 2005, leading the team through one of its most transformative periods. He made his Test debut at Lord's in 1996 with a century, earning the nickname "Dada." After retiring from international cricket, he served as BCCI president from 2019 to 2022 and currently heads the Cricket Association of Bengal.
nri_angle: Sourav Ganguly is one of the most recognizable Indian sports figures globally, and threats against him and his family are of direct concern to the Indian diaspora.
